title: Cellular Biomechanics & Mechanobiology
description: Connect forces, matrix mechanics, cell adhesion, mechanotransduction, and quantitative assays across molecular-to-tissue scales.

prerequisites.statement: Cell biology; Physics: Mechanics; Differential Equations recommended

outcomes.description: Translate boundary conditions into stress and strain measures.
Interpret viscoelastic and nonlinear material behavior.
Connect integrin/cytoskeletal signaling to mechanical context.
Design an experiment that separates stiffness from ligand density.

lesson_objectives.description: Distinguish force, stress, displacement, and strain.
Select a constitutive model appropriate to the time and strain regime.
Trace a force path from extracellular matrix to nucleus.
Predict how adhesion geometry changes local signaling.
Distinguish a mechanical input from a molecular readout.
Use perturbation and rescue to support a pathway mechanism.
Separate matrix mechanics from ligand presentation and geometry.
Choose analysis that respects nested replicates and batch structure.
Estimate an apparent Young's modulus from an indentation force and depth with the Hertz model for a spherical tip, stating its assumptions.
Calculate stress relaxation and the relaxation time for a Maxwell element and the instantaneous and long-time moduli of a standard linear solid.
Evaluate why reported cell moduli differ between methods and loading rates, and what must be reported for a value to be comparable.
Design a factorial experiment that varies stiffness and ligand density independently, with the measurements needed to confirm each factor.
Calculate main effects and an interaction effect from a 2×2 factorial and interpret them.
Convert a surface ligand density into molecules per area and spacing, and estimate total traction force from traction stress and adhesion area.
Compute the storage modulus, loss modulus, loss tangent and phase angle of a Maxwell element at a given frequency.
Identify the crossover frequency and relate the moduli to the relaxation time of a gel.
Evaluate what an oscillatory measurement shows and what must be reported with a gel modulus for a cell experiment.
Compute the bending stiffness of a cylindrical pillar and the force and traction stress from a measured deflection.
Use the scaling of the stiffness with the pillar's diameter and height to design an array.
Evaluate the limits of the beam model and of pillars as a model of a continuous substrate.
Compute a bond's lifetime under force from the Bell relation and the force at which it halves.
Compute the loading time on a substrate of given stiffness and compare it with the bond lifetime.
Evaluate a critical stiffness from the comparison and the limits of this simple clutch picture.
Compute a cortical tension from the threshold aspiration pressure and the pipette and cell radii.
Predict how the threshold pressure changes with the tension, the pipette radius and the cell radius.
Evaluate the assumptions of the liquid-drop model and what it cannot distinguish.
Compute the response at a given stiffness, and the stiffness for a given response, with a Hill function.
Interpret the maximal response, the half-maximal stiffness and the steepness, and the slope at the midpoint.
Evaluate how the choice of stiffness levels determines what an experiment can show.
Compute engineering strain, true strain, transverse strain and area strain for a stretched membrane.
Compute the stress and total force from a modulus and a strain, and the strain rate of a cyclic stretch.
Evaluate what a reported strain does and does not specify about the mechanical condition of the cells.
Summarize cell-level values to gel means for each condition of a crossed design.
Estimate the main effects and the interaction of stiffness and ligand density from the condition means.
Compare gel-level and cell-level standard errors and state what the design supports.
Quantify the loss of precision caused by two correlated explanatory variables.
Compute a diffusion coefficient from a photobleaching recovery time and use it to characterize ligand mobility.
Plan a crossed design and its replication, with the gel as the independent unit.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week undergraduate scope only. The four compact prototype units sit in weeks 1, 5, 8 and 10 beside original lessons on applying strain, indentation and relaxation, oscillatory rheology, micropillar traction forces, bonds under force, cortical tension, stiffness dose-response and factorial design; week 13 is a synthetic-data lab on stiffness, ligand density and the unit of analysis and week 14 a lesson on redesigning the stiffness experiment, which prepares the course case. All activities are open, ungraded practice. There are no graded homework sets, exams or project, and workload has not been measured, so this schedule is not evidence of semester equivalence.

lessons.title: Stress, strain, and constitutive behavior
lessons.worked_example: A standard linear solid can relax toward a nonzero long-time modulus, unlike a Maxwell element that relaxes fully under an ideal step strain.

lessons.title: Adhesion, cytoskeleton, and force transmission
lessons.worked_example: A stiffer substrate can increase traction only under conditions where cells can engage and remodel adhesions; stiffness alone does not specify cell fate.

lessons.title: Mechanotransduction and mechanosensitive pathways
lessons.worked_example: If inhibiting a mechanosensitive channel blocks calcium entry and a downstream transcriptional response, channel-specific rescue or an orthogonal perturbation strengthens the causal chain.

lessons.title: Experimental design for cell mechanics
lessons.worked_example: A 2×2 stiffness-by-ligand-density design estimates both main effects and interaction, provided each combination is independently fabricated and randomized across runs.

lessons.title: Measuring how stiff a cell is: Hertz indentation, viscoelastic relaxation and what a single modulus hides
lessons.worked_example: A 0.3 nN force at 0.5 μm with a 2.5 μm sphere gives E ≈ 302 Pa; a Maxwell element with τ = 2.0 s relaxes 100 Pa to 8.2 Pa in 5 s; a standard linear solid reads 1200 Pa fast and 400 Pa slow.

lessons.title: Separating substrate stiffness from ligand density: factorial design, interaction effects and traction forces
lessons.worked_example: In the synthetic 2×2 the stiffness main effect is 900 μm², the ligand main effect 800 μm² and the interaction 400 μm²; 10⁻¹² mol/cm² is 6022 molecules/μm² (about 13 nm apart); 300 Pa over 1000 μm² is 300 nN.

lessons.title: Oscillatory rheology: storage and loss moduli of a viscoelastic gel
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic standard linear solid with G₁ 400 Pa, G₂ 800 Pa and τ 2 s has G′ = 431 Pa at 0.1 rad/s and 1192 Pa at 5 rad/s, so its apparent stiffness depends on the frequency by a factor of about three; a Maxwell element with G 1000 Pa and τ 2 s has its crossover at 0.5 rad/s, where G′ = G″ = 500 Pa.

lessons.title: Traction forces from micropillars: force from deflection, and what the substrate really is
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic pillar with E 1.5 MPa, d 1 μm and L 4 μm has k = 3.45 nN/μm, so a 0.05 μm deflection is a force of 0.17 nN and a stress of 220 Pa, and 25 such pillars carry 4 nN; the lesson's 2 μm by 6 μm pillar has k = 21.8 nN/μm, and doubling its diameter makes it 16 times stiffer.

lessons.title: Bonds under force and rigidity sensing: lifetimes, loading rates and the molecular clutch
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic bond with τ₀ 2 s and x_b 0.8 nm lives 0.449 s at 8 pN (its lifetime halves at 3.71 pN) and, with a retrograde flow of 80 nm/s, loads to 8 pN before breaking only on substrates stiffer than 0.223 pN/nm; the lesson's bond has k_s* = 0.322 pN/nm for 10 pN at 100 nm/s.

lessons.title: Cortical tension and micropipette aspiration: a surface-tension model of a whole cell
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic cell of radius 6 μm in a 3 μm pipette with a threshold of 60 Pa has a cortical tension of 0.18 mN/m, and a cell with 0.15 mN/m would need 50 Pa; the lesson's cell (8 μm in a 4 μm pipette at 100 Pa) has 0.40 mN/m.

lessons.title: Dose–response to stiffness: the Hill function, the half-maximal stiffness and how to choose the levels
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic marker with y_max 60%, EC₅₀ 4 kPa and n 3 responds 6.7% at 2 kPa and 53.3% at 8 kPa and needs 5.77 kPa for 45%; the lesson's marker (y_max 80%, EC₅₀ 10 kPa, n 2) has a midpoint slope of 4 points per kPa, and linearly spaced levels from 20 to 100 kPa would span only 15.2 points.

lessons.title: Applying strain to cells: engineering and true strain, Poisson contraction and strain rate
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic membrane stretched 1.5 mm over 30 mm has an engineering strain of 0.050, an area strain of 0.0237, a stress of 50 kPa and a force of 0.240 N, and a 0.5 Hz cycle of amplitude 0.04 has a peak strain rate of 0.126 per second; the lesson's 10% uniaxial stretch changes the area by 0.045, against 0.21 for an equibiaxial stretch of the same size.

modules.title: Virtual laboratory: stiffness and ligand density

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: stiffness, ligand density and the unit of analysis
lessons.worked_example: In the synthetic crossed design the main effect of stiffness is 30, the ligand effect is 26 at 100 kPa and 6 at 1 kPa (interaction 10), and the gel-level standard error of the ligand effect at 100 kPa is 4.90 against a naive cell-level 2.32.

lessons.title: Decoupling stiffness from ligand density and mobility: redesigning the experiment
lessons.worked_example: Two predictors correlated at r = 0.9 give a variance inflation of 5.26; with a between-gel SD of 5, a within-gel SD of 12, 15 cells per gel and 6 gels per arm, the gel-level standard error is 3.40 against a naive cell-level 1.94; a 4 μm spot recovering in 20 s gives D = 0.179 μm²/s; the lesson's r = 0.95 gives a variance inflation of 10.26 and a gel-level standard error of 3.24.

assessments.title: Virtual lab 1: stiffness, ligand density and the unit of analysis (ungraded practice)

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (Hertz indentation and viscoelastic relaxation; separating substrate stiffness from ligand density with a factorial design and traction forces) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a proposed 14-week schedule; seven original lessons (oscillatory rheology and the storage and loss moduli; micropillar traction forces; bonds under force and the molecular clutch; cortical tension and micropipette aspiration; the Hill function and stiffness dose-response; applying strain to cells; and decoupling stiffness from ligand density, which prepares the course case); and a synthetic-data lab on stiffness, ligand density and the unit of analysis. No new references were added. All activities remain ungraded practice; the package remains partial and unreviewed, gives no laboratory protocol or handling procedure, and makes no claim about any cell, gel or measurement.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved beside ten original readings, including one synthetic-data virtual lab; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.

A proposed 14-week schedule exists but is unmeasured and unreviewed. There is one synthetic-data virtual lab and no substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.

Practice items are short formative checks (two per prototype unit and six to nine per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 62 numerical answers in this package, twelve require a unit, one checks significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.

All gels, cells, forces and numbers are synthetic teaching examples; this package gives no laboratory protocols, handling procedures or medical advice and says nothing about any real cell type, material or measurement. The models are simplified textbook descriptions, not analysis methods for real data.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments and a laboratory sequence are not authored yet (one synthetic-data virtual lab exists); the original lessons extend a partial package.
